desc:
A directed network has n nodes labelled 0 to n - 1. Each edges[i] = [from, to, w] is a one-way edge of weight w, which may be negative.

Return true if the network contains a cycle whose total weight is strictly negative and that can be reached from node src (that is, some node of the cycle is reachable from src, which means all of them are). Otherwise return false. A cycle of total weight exactly 0 does not count, and a negative cycle that src can never reach does not count either. A self-loop [v, v, w] is a cycle of one edge.

Example: n = 3, edges = [[0,1,1],[1,2,-2],[2,1,1]], src = 0. The cycle 1 → 2 → 1 has weight -2 + 1 = -1 and is reachable, so the answer is true. If the last edge had weight 2 the cycle would total 0 and the answer would be false.
constraints: edges[i] = [from, to, w] with 0 ≤ from, to < n and -1,000 ≤ w ≤ 1,000
Each ordered pair (from, to) appears at most once; from may equal to
hints: If shortest distances from src were well defined, they would stop changing after enough rounds of relaxing all edges. What happens when a negative cycle is reachable?
Relax all edges n - 1 times, only from nodes that already have a finite distance. A shortest simple route has at most n - 1 edges, so without a reachable negative cycle everything is final by then.

Do one more pass. If any edge can still be relaxed (dist[u] + w < dist[v] with dist[u] finite), a negative cycle is reachable from src; return true. Nodes with no route from src must be ignored, otherwise unreachable negative cycles cause false alarms.
editorial: This is the standard Bellman-Ford negative cycle test. Start with dist[src] = 0 and infinity elsewhere and relax every edge n - 1 times, skipping edges that start at an unreached node. If no negative cycle is reachable, then each shortest route is a simple path of at most n - 1 edges, so all distances are final after those passes and an n-th pass changes nothing. If a reachable negative cycle exists, its total weight is below zero, so the sum of the relaxation inequalities around it cannot all hold: at least one edge of the cycle is still relaxable in the n-th pass.

The condition 'reachable from src' is what the infinity guard implements: unreached nodes keep infinite distance and never relax anything, so a negative cycle in a different component is invisible, as the problem requires. Zero-weight cycles never allow a strict improvement and are not reported. Time is O(n · E), space O(n). Floyd-Warshall with a check for d[i][i] < 0 also finds negative cycles but in O(n3) and it would need an extra reachability test.
